line: From a sweet stall that poisoned a whole town, to a candy that can quietly stop your heart.
These are the deadliest sweets ever sold.
title: THE DEADLIEST | SWEETS | EVER SOLD

line: And we're starting in England, in eighteen fifty-eight.
These are peppermint humbugs, striped little hard sweets sold from market stalls all over Victorian England.
title: A VICTORIAN MARKET CLASSIC
name: PEPPERMINT HUMBUGS

line: They were cheap, they were everywhere, and kids loved them.
visual: A pile of striped black and white peppermint humbug hard sweets on an old wooden market table

line: In the town of Bradford, one sweet seller had a problem.
Sugar was expensive, so sweet makers bulked it up with a cheap white powder called daff.
title: CUTTING CORNERS
rows: SUGAR = EXPENSIVE; BULK IT UP; DAFF = CHEAP FILLER

line: It wasn't tasty, but it wasn't going to hurt anyone either.
But one day the chemist's assistant reached into the wrong barrel, and handed over arsenic instead.
title: THE CHEMIST'S SHOP

line: Arsenic trioxide is a white powder that looks almost exactly like sugar.
Nobody noticed. It went straight into the pot, and the sweets went on sale that same week.
visual: A Victorian sweet maker stirring a big copper pot of boiling sugar in a dim candle-lit workshop, 1850s England

line: Around twenty people died, and more than two hundred fell seriously ill.
At first, doctors blamed a disease going around town. It wasn't a disease.
Ten years later, Britain passed the Pharmacy Act, so poisons had to be labelled and sold only by trained chemists.
title: WHAT CHANGED
rows: 1858 = BRADFORD POISONING; 1868 = PHARMACY ACT; TODAY = POISONS LABELLED !green

line: But nobody ever went to prison for it.
Still, at least arsenic worked fast, because this next sweet takes its time.
title: IT TAKES ITS TIME...

line: This is black liquorice, the one candy everybody has an opinion about.
title: THE CANDY AISLE CLASSIC
name: BLACK LIQUORICE

line: In twenty twenty, doctors in Massachusetts wrote up the case of a man who ate a bag and a half of it every day.
title: THE CASE REPORT
rows: PATIENT = 54-YEAR-OLD CONSTRUCTION WORKER; HABIT = A BAG AND A HALF A DAY; OUTCOME = HIS HEART STOPPED

line: Real black liquorice gets its flavour from liquorice root.
The root it's made from drains your potassium, and your heart needs potassium to keep a steady beat.
title: WHAT LIQUORICE ROOT DOES
rows: candy = LIQUORICE ROOT; down = POTASSIUM DROPS; heart = HEARTBEAT GOES HAYWIRE

line: So yeah, a little is fine. A bag and a half a day? Maybe not.
